BUCKLEY CLIMATE SEQUENCE | EXISTING ANGKOR MODEL

Data: NOAA Bidoup Nui Ba National Park PDSI reconstruction, Buckley et al.
2010. The supplied subset is 1250–1450, with 201 consecutive annual rows.
https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/paleo/treering/reconstructions/asia/vietnam/bidoup-nui-ba2010pdsi.txt
Publication: https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0910827107
Retrieved 7 November 2026. The CSV subset was extracted from NOAA's
plain-text data as returned by the web reader. PDSI is a regional
March–May drought proxy, rather than annual rainfall at Angkor.

This is Buckley's published climate sequence driving our existing
longrun2 model. Buckley and Lieberman's papers do not supply the social
model implemented here. All six historical-driver switches are off.
The background succession process remains. Before 1250 each paired
run keeps the same original synthetic weather and initialization.

Three climate-response sensitivities are run with 2,000 matched parameter
draws each, plus 2,000 neutral-climate controls. For sensitivity s:
weather factor = min(1.15, max(0.4, 1 + PDSI * s)).
The code's existing hydraulic buffering still applies.
The coefficient and clipping are model assumptions, not a calibration.
Positive PDSI values are not converted to hydraulic flood damage.

Results:
Sensitivity   Sustained core decline / 2000    Median onset among those
0             0                              —
.04           217                            1402
.07           1260                           1362
.10           1657                           1338

At .07, the median 1450 core and regional populations are both 89.4%
of their 1300 values. The core remains defined by court presence times
regional population in this older engine. The paper's historical
land-use chronology has not been fitted here.

To rerun with Node:
  node run.cjs > results.csv

The driver verifies complete annual coverage and checks population
and infrastructure bounds. Read the driver to see the exact weather
replacement in the unchanged source engine.
